senses.gloss: An offensive word for a person who has lost brain function and can no longer move or respond.
examples: Calling a patient a *vegetable* is cruel, and most doctors refuse to do it.
He was terrified that the stroke would leave him a *vegetable*.
Families object when the news calls coma patients *vegetables*.

senses.gloss: A spot beside a road or trail where people stop to look at the scenery.
examples: We pulled off at a *viewpoint* to watch the sun go down over the canyon.
There are three marked *viewpoints* along the rim trail.
The *viewpoint* has a small parking lot and a coin-operated telescope.

senses.gloss: A picture whose edges fade gradually into the background, or the darkening around the edges of a photograph.
examples: Her great-grandmother's portrait is a soft *vignette* in an oval frame.
I added a slight *vignette* to pull the eye toward her face.
Cheap lenses often leave a dark *vignette* in the corners of the shot.

senses.gloss: The amount of public attention that something or someone receives.
examples: The lawsuit gave the issue national *visibility*.
She took the job for the *visibility* it would give her career.
The brand has almost no *visibility* outside the Northeast.

senses.gloss: A gathering at a funeral home where people come to see the body and comfort the family before the funeral.
senses.ru: прощание с покойным (в похоронном бюро накануне похорон)
examples: *Visitation* will be Thursday from six to eight at Miller Funeral Home.
Close to two hundred people came to the *visitation*.
We drove up for the *visitation* and stayed through the burial the next day.

senses.gloss: The phone service that records messages when you cannot answer.
examples: Her *voicemail* is full, so I texted her instead.
I still haven't set up *voicemail* on the new phone.
I called twice and it went straight to *voicemail* both times.

senses.gloss: A plant that comes up on its own from a seed nobody planted.
examples: That tomato is a *volunteer* from last year's compost pile.
We left the sunflower *volunteers* standing along the fence.
Half the pumpkins in the patch this year were *volunteers*.

senses.gloss: A weak point in a computer system that an attacker can use to break in.
examples: Researchers found a *vulnerability* in the bank's login page.
The update patches four serious *vulnerabilities*.
The *vulnerability* let anyone read other users' files.

senses.gloss: The picture set as the background on a computer or phone screen.
examples: He changed his *wallpaper* to a photo of his dog.
The default *wallpaper* on the new laptop is a mountain at dawn.
I keep different *wallpapers* on my phone and my work computer.

senses.gloss: All the clothes that one person owns.
examples: She got rid of half her *wardrobe* before the move.
A good coat is worth the money even if the rest of your *wardrobe* is cheap.
He built his whole work *wardrobe* around two gray suits.

senses.gloss: A person or organization that keeps watch on a company or a government and reports bad behavior.
examples: A consumer *watchdog* sued the airline over hidden fees.
The agency is supposed to be a *watchdog*, not a partner.
Ethics *watchdogs* filed a complaint against the governor last week.

senses.gloss: A logo or words laid faintly over a digital image or document to show who owns it or that it is not final.
examples: The preview photos all have the studio's *watermark* across them.
You have to pay to download the file without the *watermark*.
Every page of the draft carries a gray DRAFT *watermark*.

senses.gloss: A sudden sharp change or reversal that leaves people shaken.
examples: The constant changes to the rules gave teachers *whiplash*.
Investors got *whiplash* from two rate cuts in a single month.
Ninety degrees one week and snow the next is weather *whiplash*.

senses.gloss: A tub of hot water with jets, used for relaxing or for treating a sore muscle or joint.
examples: The trainer had him soak his ankle in the *whirlpool*.
The hotel room came with a *whirlpool* in the bathroom.
After practice half the team was sitting in the *whirlpool*.

senses.gloss: The act of pulling out of a place or taking something back, especially of troops leaving a country.
examples: The *withdrawal* of American troops took eighteen months.
His *withdrawal* from the race surprised everyone at the party.
The company announced its *withdrawal* from the European market.

senses.gloss: The sick, shaky period a person goes through after quitting a drug the body has come to depend on.
examples: He spent three days in *withdrawal* before the worst of it passed.
Caffeine *withdrawal* gave her a headache for most of a week.
The clinic treats *withdrawal* with medication and counseling.

senses.gloss: A short class in which a small group practices a skill together.
examples: She's teaching a two-day *workshop* on résumé writing.
I signed up for a pottery *workshop* at the community center.
Fifteen people came to the first *workshop* and only six to the second.

senses.gloss: A standard used for judging or comparing things.
examples: Test scores are a poor *yardstick* for a good teacher.
By any *yardstick*, last season was a success.
Profit is not the only *yardstick* this company uses.
